relevance.rationale: The document proves a conjectured family of inequalities for truncated sums involving b_6(n), the number of 6-regular partitions of n, using a Cayley formula for partitions into parts at most 3, in the tradition of truncated theorems on Euler's pentagonal number theorem. This is additive partition combinatorics. Corpus greps for '6-regular', 'regular partition' and 'truncated pentagonal' return nothing across content/, computations/ and docs/. The corpus's only contact with additive partition counting is p(n) itself, in a8-partition-function-identity (a_8(X) = sum p(n) X^{5-n} for n = 1..5, with p(1..5) = 1,2,3,5,7); nothing there needs b_6(n), a truncated series, or an inequality. Elsewhere 'partition' in this corpus means a Young-diagram index lambda for a Wedderburn block — a homonym, not the same object. Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing usable here. That is not a claim that partition combinatorics is irrelevant to the folio.
